name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,772

entries.clue: This man's covered with paint at work (8)

annotation.definition: This man's covered with paint at work

indicatorNotes.covered with: something covered with a coat has that coat all round it, so the jumbled PAINT wraps round HE'S
indicatorNotes.at work: letters at work are busy moving about, so PAINT's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: PAINT rearranged, wrapped round the next piece
this man's = HE'S, sitting inside after the T

annotation.surface: An actor in greasepaint, busy on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: a man working with paint all over him is exactly an actor in stage make-up.
annotation.definitionFit: Read straight, the clue describes an actor on stage in greasepaint, and thespian is a slightly grand word for an actor, after Thespis of ancient Greece.

entries.clue: What well-behaved prisoner does as often as not (4,3,4)

blocks.note: good behaviour can earn release after serving only part of a sentence
an idiom for 'on roughly one occasion in two'

annotation.surface: A model inmate earning remission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time' is prison slang for a sentence, so a well-behaved prisoner may do only half the time; the same phrase is the everyday idiom for 'as often as not'.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is literal, a prisoner serving half a sentence of time; the other is the idiom for something happening on about every second occasion.

entries.clue: Female sex matter (7)

annotation.surface: A phrase that sounds like a tabloid headline about women and sex.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Matter' is the noun, as in 'the whole shebang' meaning the whole affair or business.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: shebang means an affair or business, almost always heard in the idiom 'the whole shebang'.

entries.clue: Wearing cool hat like the kids (9)

blocks.note: in = wearing, as in 'in a hat'
tile = an old slang word for a hat

annotation.surface: Someone in a trendy hat trying to look young.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cool' looks like an adjective describing the hat, but it is the verb: to fan.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: infantile comes from infant, so it describes behaviour typical of small children.

entries.clue: Educate form in hours (7)

indicatorNotes.form: to form something is to shape it, so the letters of IN HOURS are shaped into a new word

annotation.surface: A school timetable: teaching the form during lesson hours.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Form' looks like a school class to be taught; it is the verb telling you to rearrange 'in hours'.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: feeding the mind, as in nourishing a child's talents, is a way of bringing up and educating.

entries.clue: Republican in raincoat running for President (6)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the Republican literally inside the raincoat, so R sits inside MAC

blocks.note: on = running, as a machine is

annotation.surface: A Republican candidate in a raincoat campaigning for the presidency.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Republican' and 'running for President' point to an American election; the President meant is French.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Emmanuel Macron has held the office of President of France since 2017.

entries.clue: On board, beaten seaman died (5)

blocks.note: a mate is a ship's officer
d. = died, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A sailor beaten up on board ship who then died.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; the board is a chessboard, where a mated king is beaten.
annotation.definitionFit: A chess sense: a player checkmated has lost, beaten on the board, and 'on board' pins the sense to the game.

entries.clue: Embarrassment when cleaner at home hoovers dog's tail (7)

indicatorNotes.hoovers: to hoover is to vacuum something up, so CHAR sucks G inside itself
indicatorNotes.tail: an animal's tail is its hind end, so a word's tail is its last letter

blocks.note: a char is a cleaning lady
last letter of dog, inside CHAR

annotation.surface: An awkward moment when the cleaner vacuums up part of the dog.
annotation.walkthrough: A char (charwoman or charlady) is a British word for a woman paid to clean houses; to hoover is British for to vacuum.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: chagrin is the vexed embarrassment of being made to look foolish, borrowed from French.

entries.clue: Lyric sounded outstanding (3)

indicatorNotes.sounded: a word sounded is spoken out, so the answer matches the sound of the word for 'outstanding', not its spelling

annotation.surface: A song that sounded excellent.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' suggests excellent; here it means still unpaid.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a lyric is a short poem expressing feeling, and an ode is one kind of lyric poem, often addressed to its subject.

entries.clue: Britain left European Union, turning to the right (4)

indicatorNotes.turning: something turning round faces the other way, so EU is read backwards

annotation.surface: Brexit as a lurch in politics: Britain quits the EU and moves rightwards.
annotation.walkthrough: In British politics blue is the colour of the Conservative Party, so blue means right-wing.
annotation.definitionFit: A British political sense: the Conservatives' colour is blue, so a blue voter or seat leans to the right.

entries.clue: Fellow regretted keeping guitar, not getting it (10)

indicatorNotes.keeping: to keep something is to hold it, so RUED holds STRAT inside

blocks.note: Strat = the Fender Stratocaster, inside RUED

annotation.surface: A man who wishes he had never kept the guitar he never learned to play.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not getting it' reads as failing to understand; it means not getting what one wants, often sexual satisfaction.
annotation.definitionFit: A colloquial sense: someone frustrated is thwarted, not getting the satisfaction they want, with a knowing sexual hint.

entries.clue: Cheers on cheers reflected popular win (6)

indicatorNotes.reflected: a reflection in a mirror runs backwards, so TA becomes AT

annotation.surface: A crowd cheering again and again for a popular victory.
annotation.walkthrough: Ta is British for thanks, one sense of 'cheers'. The first TA sits 'on' (after) the reversed one.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to win a prize or a goal by effort is to attain it.

entries.clue: Charge around on roundabout (8)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means surrounding, so INDICT surrounds RE

blocks.note: to indict is to charge with a crime

annotation.surface: A car speeding round a traffic roundabout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' is the traffic circle in the surface but the adjective in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: a roundabout route or remark goes the long way, not straight to the point.

entries.clue: Charlie chokes up collecting prize, for star pupil? (6,5)

indicatorNotes.collecting: to collect something is to take it in, so C CLOGS takes LEVER inside

blocks.note: C = Charlie in the phonetic alphabet
to prize (prise) something open is to lever it

annotation.surface: A boy named Charlie gets emotional when collecting a school prize.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prize' is the verb (prise open), not an award. Clever clogs is a British term for a know-all, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a star pupil is the sort of child classmates tease as a clever clogs, British slang for a smart alec.

entries.clue: All in Schengen upset about Hungary's immigration barrier (7,7)

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is knocked over, so the letters of ALL IN SCHENGEN are rearranged
indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around, so the jumbled letters go around H, taking it into the mix

blocks.note: H is Hungary's international vehicle registration code

annotation.surface: European politics: Schengen members upset over Hungary's border fence.
annotation.walkthrough: The Schengen area is the EU zone without internal border checks; Britain stayed out, and the Channel is its natural barrier to migrants.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: the stretch of sea between England and France is what migrants in small boats must cross, so it acts as a barrier.

entries.clue: Cold shower affected army's devotions (4,5)

indicatorNotes.affected: something affected is changed, so the letters of ARMY'S are altered into a new order

blocks.note: hail is a cold shower of ice

annotation.surface: Soldiers' prayers disrupted by freezing wet weather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cold shower' suggests a bathroom; it is weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Hail Mary is a Catholic prayer to the Virgin Mary, and prayers are devotions.

entries.clue: Wee-wee in dribbles (6,2,6)

blocks.note: the surface pushes a childish word for urinating; read it as 'wee' (small) said twice over
the surface means trickles of urine; the setter means gradually, a small amount at a time

annotation.surface: A bodily function performed a trickle at a time.
annotation.walkthrough: Wee is Scottish and British for small as well as for urine; the answer is 'wee' by 'wee' in its other sense, and 'in dribbles' means gradually.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: little by little means gradually, in small instalments, and here the two 'wee's supply the two littles.

entries.clue: Learner taxiing regularly in plane, say (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so take every other letter of 'taxiing'
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places those letters inside the tree

blocks.note: a plane is a kind of tree

annotation.surface: A learner pilot taxiing an aircraft along the runway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plane' is the aircraft in the surface and the tree (London plane) in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trainee is someone being taught a job, a learner.

entries.clue: Tongue lifted home-made meal (7)

indicatorNotes.lifted: in a down clue something lifted goes up, so DIY reads from bottom to top

annotation.surface: Someone lifting a home-cooked meal to their tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tongue' looks like the organ of taste; it means a language.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: tongue means language, and Yiddish is the language of Ashkenazi Jews.

entries.clue: Fox and wolf beginning to hunt excessively (2,5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here the H of 'hunt'

blocks.note: tod = a dialect word for a fox
to wolf food is to eat it greedily

annotation.surface: A fox and a wolf setting out on a hunt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wolf' is the verb, to gobble; tod is an old word for a fox, seen in names like Todd.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'bored to death' or 'done to death' uses the phrase as an intensifier meaning to an excessive degree.

entries.clue: During charitable gala I donated money for cause (5,3)

indicatorNotes.During: something during an event happens within it, so the answer lies within the words that follow

annotation.surface: A donor giving money at a charity gala for a good cause.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cause' looks like a charity; it is a legal case, as in 'cause list'.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: legal aid is state money paying for someone's lawsuit, and a cause is an old word for a court case.

entries.clue: Amateur with aim to improve (5)

blocks.note: an end = an aim or goal

annotation.surface: An amateur with the ambition to get better.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins AM and END.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: you amend a text or law to put right its faults, which improves it.

entries.clue: Cold duck on sea current gives quack (6)

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, shaped like O

annotation.surface: A cold duck bobbing on an ocean current and quacking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quack' is the duck's call in the surface but slang for a doctor. C and O sit 'on' (after) MED and I.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang for slang: quack is jokey or scornful slang for a doctor, and medico is another informal word for one.

entries.clue: Light fitting in reach stupidly broken by Trotter (10)

indicatorNotes.stupidly: done stupidly means done in a muddled way, so IN REACH is jumbled
indicatorNotes.broken by: something broken by an intruder is split open, so DEL is inserted among the jumbled letters

annotation.surface: Something within reach of a clumsy pig, which breaks it.
annotation.walkthrough: Del Boy Trotter is the hero of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, in a famous scene where a chandelier falls and smashes.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a chandelier is one kind of light fitting, a branched frame of lamps hung from the ceiling.

entries.clue: Wrap up warmly? (3)

blocks.note: the surface means put on layers of clothes; the setter means enfold someone in your arms
the surface means against the cold; the setter means affectionately

annotation.surface: Advice to dress warmly for cold weather.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up warmly' is the advice to put on a coat; the question mark flags that 'warmly' here means with affection.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: to wrap someone up in your arms with affection is exactly what a hug does.

entries.clue: Curry ingredient in a can (4)

blocks.note: can and loo are both slang for a toilet

annotation.surface: A tinned curry ingredient.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a tin; it is American slang for the toilet, and loo is the British word.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: aloo is Hindi for potato, used in curries such as aloo gobi.

entries.clue: Silver vibrator decided upon jointly (6)

blocks.note: Ag = the chemical symbol for silver
a reed vibrates to make the sound in a clarinet or oboe

annotation.surface: A saucy picture of a silver sex toy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Vibrator' suggests something else entirely; it is the reed of a wind instrument.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as past participles: terms agreed are ones the parties have settled together.

entries.clue: Secret still repeated (4-4)

indicatorNotes.repeated: something repeated is said again, so the word for 'still' appears twice in a row

blocks.note: to hush is to still or silence

annotation.surface: A secret that someone keeps telling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Still' is a verb here, to quieten, not the adverb.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: something hush-hush is kept quiet, the doubled 'hush' echoing a call for silence.
